chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever interrupts his Muslim brother while he is speaking in his discourse, it is as if he has scratched his face.'

key_terms.الْمُتَكَلِّمِ فِي حَدِيثِهِ: the one speaking in his discourse
key_terms.خَدَشَ: to scratch or scratch the surface

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for interrupting someone who is speaking?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi through the chain of al-Sakuni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the spiritual gravity of interrupting a speaker, equating it to physically marrying their face. This metaphor highlights the violation of the listener's dignity and the disruption of the flow of beneficial knowledge, a key theme in Shia etiquette of speech (adab al-kalam). It serves as a practical guideline for maintaining respect during religious discourse and daily interactions.
